title: Waypoint supplychain outbound scratch
content:
Quick persona sketch and problem framing:

- Company: Waypoint SupplyChain (mid-market, global freight forwarder + customs brokerage). HQ: Rotterdam, large EU operation, expanding US west coast consolidation hubs.
- Key buyers: Head of Digital (Arjan de Vries), Director of Ops (Priya Rao), Platform Eng lead (Diego Alvarez).
- Buying signals: public note about modernization/observability, recent funding (Series B, Oct 2025), job posts for ML infra / automation.
- Pain to target: messy exceptions in shipment tracking (customs delays, carrier status ambiguity), high CS load handling ETA questions, manual claim processing.

Why Redwood could matter (high-level):
- Embeddings/search for shipment events + semantic reranking to reduce false positives in exception alerts.
- Low-latency chat for CS agents and self-service LLM for customers with compliance for PII (Private deployment ask).
- Dedicated capacity for predictable throughput during booking spikes and nightly consolidation runs.

Quick account map (rough):
- Arjan de Vries — Head of Digital (evaluation lead, cares about integrations + time-to-value).
- Priya Rao — Director Ops (pilot champion for CS reduction metrics).
- Diego Alvarez — Platform Eng (security + deployment constraints; will ask about VPC/KMS).
- Procurement: contacts unknown — expect an SOW/contract review.

Initial outreach hypotheses / subject lines to A/B test:
A: "Cut Waypoint's ETA exception volume by 30% — quick pilot?"
B: "Reduce CS handling time for customs problems (pilot idea)"
C: "Small pilot: AI assistant for freight ops — 2 week setup"

Cold email skeleton (version A):
Hi Arjan —
I’m Maya from Redwood Inference. We help freight/platform teams reduce manual exception handling by combining fast, private LLM inference with semantic search over events and documents.
We recently ran a pilot with a logistics operator that cut agent touchpoints by ~28% by surfacing the right carrier docs and auto-drafting claim responses.
Would you be open to a 20‑minute call to see if a similar small pilot (2–4 routes, UAT with CS) makes sense?
— Maya

Call prep notes (if we get a discovery):
- Ask about current event model: EDI + carrier webhooks? frequency of status updates?
- What does "exception" mean for them (customs hold, missing docs, damaged, ETA drift)?
- Current CS volume per week for these cases and average handle time.
- Security constraints: can they accept a private deployment or need on-prem? KMS/HSM reqs?
- Success criteria: % reduction in manual touches, MTTR on exceptions, accuracy of suggested doc templates.

Pilot framing (MVP scope):
- 2–4 routes (EU -> US west + NL inland)
- Ingest 30 days of events + 5000 most recent shipment records (S3 or signed link)
- Endpoint: agent-facing chat + reranking API used by ops UI
- Duration: 4 weeks (2 week setup, 2 week evaluation)
- Target metrics: 25–35% reduction in manual ticket volume; >70% precision on suggested claim templates.
- Pricing (very rough internal): Hosted pilot: $12k/mo credits + optional dedicated pool for bursts; Private pilot (VPC) add-on: implementation fee $18k + infra run rate TBD.

Objections & rapid rebuttals (prep language):
- "We can't send PII to a vendor." -> "We can do a Private deployment into your VPC or on-prem with customer-managed KMS. We also support token filtering and local redaction hooks during ingestion."
- "Latency matters for our UI." -> "We can run a dedicated capacity with targeted latency SLOs; Redwood supports continuous batching and K/V cache to keep 95th percentile sub-100ms for agent queries in dedicated setups."
- "We already built an internal model." -> "Totally—teams often keep model dev and use Redwood for reliable, predictable serving and rollout controls. We can host your model privately and provide observability and safe rollouts."
- "Pricing / procurement cycles are slow." -> "Start with a small hosted pilot (credits) to prove ROI before procurement. We can convert to committed Dedicated capacity if it scales."

Success signals to monitor in pilot:
- Reduction in number of escalations to Ops (weekly)
- CS response time for customs holds (avg/95th)
- Precision of suggested templates and false positive rate
- Developer integration effort (time-to-first-call)

Next steps (internal):
- Samir to draft tailored one-pager that calls out customs-specific examples (due: 2026-03-07).
- Ella to prepare an embedding + reranking mini-demo using synthetic EDI payloads (runbook in GH PR #72).
- Book intro with Arjan: target week of 2026-03-15. Prep: two short demos (embedded search + agent chat), slide: "how pilot works in 30m".

Open questions / risks:
- Waypoint's willingness to produce event data for pilot (GDPR/contract constraints?).
- C-level economic sponsor — likely ops but may need CFO to sign for dedicated capacity.
- Integration surface: will they expect turnkey connectors for X12/EDIFACT? Might need connector scope.

Tiny script for cold call/VM:
"Hi Arjan — Maya at Redwood. Quick note: we help freight ops cut manual exception queues with an opinionated inference platform that your security team can run in-VPC. Sent a brief note — would love 20 minutes to discuss a low-effort pilot. Thanks"

Notes to self (keep):
- Don't oversell "self-service for customers" until we validate carrier doc ingestion reliability.
- Emphasize observability: per-route token cost breakdown & regression alerts are a big trust-builder.
- If they push on latency, have a slide that shows Dedicated + cache path and historical p95 numbers from similar customers (ask Eng for anonymized statset).

Reference links / artifacts for follow-up:
- Confluence pilot brief (linked above)
- GH proposal with sample payloads: https://github.com/redwood-inference/proposals/pull/72
- JIRA: JIRA-PS-918 (pilot scoping)

End of scratchpad.

-- Maya
